title: How Autonomous Vehicles Handle Terrain Prediction

scenes.title: Navigating Unseen Paths
scenes.narration: Autonomous vehicles must precisely understand terrain conditions, but adverse weather like snow or heavy rain severely limits traditional sensor visibility, posing a significant safety risk. This challenge is critical for reliable navigation.

scenes.title: Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion
scenes.narration: To overcome visual limitations, AVs employ multi-modal sensor fusion, combining data from diverse sources like radar, thermal cameras, and ultrasonic sensors. This creates a more robust environmental perception than any single sensor.

scenes.title: Radar & Thermal Vision
scenes.narration: Radar penetrates fog and snow to detect objects and their distance, while thermal cameras sense heat signatures, distinguishing living beings from inanimate objects regardless of light. These are crucial for adverse conditions.

scenes.title: Predictive Terrain Modeling
scenes.narration: Advanced systems use predictive modeling, leveraging historical data and real-time sensor inputs to anticipate terrain changes like icy patches or deep puddles. This allows the AV to adjust its driving strategy proactively.

scenes.title: Enhanced Safety & Reliability
scenes.narration: By integrating these advanced techniques, autonomous vehicles achieve significantly enhanced safety and reliability, enabling them to operate confidently in diverse and challenging weather conditions. This expands their operational design domain.
